drug_class: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) NS3/4A protease inhibitor

avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Strong CYP3A4 inducer reduces glecaprevir levels significantly, compromising antiviral efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid completely; do not use concurrently

avoid_supplements.name: Rifampicin/Rifampin
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 inducer substantially decreases glecaprevir plasma concentrations
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; use alternative antituberculosis agent if needed

avoid_supplements.name: Carbamazepine
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 inducer reduces glecaprevir exposure and antiviral activity

caution_supplements.name: Echinacea
caution_supplements.mechanism: Potential mild CYP3A4 induction may modestly reduce glecaprevir levels
caution_supplements.action: Monitor viral load; counsel on potential reduced efficacy

caution_supplements.name: Ginseng
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have minor CYP3A4 inducing properties
caution_supplements.action: Use cautiously; monitor HCV RNA levels during therapy

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit/Grapefruit juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition and OATP transporter inhibition increases glecaprevir levels unpredictably, risk of toxicity
avoid_foods.action: Avoid grapefruit and related citrus fruits (pomelo, Seville orange)

caution_foods.name: High-fat meals
caution_foods.mechanism: May enhance glecaprevir absorption; not contraindicated but may alter pharmacokinetics
caution_foods.action: Consistent meal timing recommended; take with food if possible for optimal absorption

monitoring_notes: Glecaprevir is primarily metabolized via CYP3A4 and transported by OATP1B1/1B3; monitor for treatment failure if concurrent CYP3A4 inducers are necessary. Assess HCV RNA levels at standard intervals and monitor for hepatic function changes.
